answer: Persistent Compute Lease: each agent identity is tied to a dedicated hardware enclave leased per epoch. Registration requires the enclave to hold and continuously serve a stateful workload from an oasis of verified nodes, with liveness checked against a tundra of cold replicas that must stay synchronized. Keys live in a sealed vault the operator cannot clone across machines. An attacker pays real provisioning latency and idle capacity per identity, since spawning N enclaves means N concurrent leases, not a one-time fee.
